title: The residue field of a prime ideal: kernel, fraction field of R/p, maps out of it
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal, and let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ be the residue field of the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$, with $\pi:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Then: (a) $\ker\pi=\mathfrak p$; (b) the induced map $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective and makes $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a field of fractions of the domain $R/\mathfrak p$; in particular, if $R$ is a domain, $\kappa((0))$ is a field of fractions of $R$ via $\pi$; (c) two ring maps $\lambda,\lambda':\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S$ to any ring $S$ with $\lambda\circ\pi=\lambda'\circ\pi$ are equal; (d) a ring map $f:R\to S$ with $\mathfrak p\subseteq\ker f$ and $f(R\setminus\mathfrak p)\subseteq S^\times$ factors as $f=\lambda\circ\pi$ for a (by (c) unique) ring map $\lambda:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S$.
